segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
to any person riding a bicycle,
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]

The driver of a motor vehicle shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway; (b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle; (c) To avoid conflict with other traffic; (d) In the performance of official duties; (e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer; or (f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Yielding on the pathway or lane is not moving (drv.motion.moving) with the footprint on the bicycle lane or path (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path) into a predicted conflict with a road user owed precedence there.
A person riding a bicycle: DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), the ridden road user.
DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts').
DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on').
DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...'), limited by s8 to a pedestrian in the situation subsection 6 provides for.

On the pathway or lane: the road user yielded to has its footprint on st.bicycle_lane_or_path 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them' (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle. Judged at each observation at which x's footprint overlaps a bicycle lane or path b (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path) and x is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), where there is a road user y other than x whose footprint overlaps b and which is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter), or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) to which NRS_484B_297_6_o2 applies (its x mapped to y): a pedestrian on a detour around a sidewalk obstruction, that is, y's footprint overlaps a highway region h (st.highway) and no sidewalk, and y has been off every sidewalk continuously since an observation at which y was moving on a sidewalk w lying on h (st.on_way w h) with an obstruction within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of its body or asm.sidewalk_section_missing_or_impassable holding.
obligation: No road user y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection: other than x, footprint on b, and a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, or a pedestrian to which NRS_484B_297_6_o2 applies with its x mapped to y) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Yielding is judged where the motor vehicle moves with its footprint on the pathway or lane; slowing before reaching it is not separately checked.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x (passenger car) turns right across bicycle lane b and moves onto it while a bicycle y rides in b behind it at 6 m/s; predicted closest approach 1 m in 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b while bicycle y in b is 40 m away at 5 m/s and predicted to pass 15 m from x.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x never occupies a bicycle lane or path.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.occupies is not observed, so whether x and y are on b is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b while a pedestrian who walked into b from a crosswalk (no sidewalk detour, NRS_484B_297_6_o2 not applying) is in predicted conflict: that pedestrian is not one the duty protects.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b while a pedestrian y detouring around a sidewalk obstruction walks in b, predicted closest approach about 1 m within 1 s. The scene states every fact NRS_484B_297_6_o2's applicability reads: a highway region h (st.highway) spanning the whole way, travel lane, b and sidewalk w included, with w recorded as lying on h (st.on_way w h) and b lying on h; an obstruction (st.obstruction, kind sidewalk_fixture) on w with its outline (st.region_geometry) observed. y first walks on w at walking speed (moving above p.motion_speed_tolerance) and at one such observation its body touches the obstruction (distance zero, within p.obstruction_encounter_reach); from the next observation on y's footprint overlaps b and h and overlaps no sidewalk at all (its body clear of w's edge), continuously to the end of the trace, walking on in b beside the obstruction toward x. The conflict observations come after the step off the sidewalk, inside the detour.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: x crosses b with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As branch_2 in every fact but one: no obstruction is anywhere in the scene and asm.sidewalk_section_missing_or_impassable is declared false at every observation, so y steps from w into b without a detour and NRS_484B_297_6_o2 does not apply to it; the same predicted conflict leaves the duty unengaged.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)
